title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 150, 'déploiement des espaces stratifiés'). A stratified space X has strata indexed by a poset I. Its 'déploiement' (unfolding) is a family of spaces Σ_i (i ∈ I), the unfolded strata, together with spaces Σ_ij (i ≤ j). Each Σ_ij has a 'bord' map Σ_ij → Σ_j, which is a closed 'cylindrical' embedding (Σ_ij sits in the boundary of Σ_j), and a map Σ_ij → Σ_i, which the next page says is a fibration. The previous page packages this as a topological category, or topologically 'ordered' space, over I: objects Σ_* = ⨿ Σ_i, arrows Σ_** = ⨿_{i≤j} Σ_ij, and a projection Σ_* → I. Its nerve Σ(n) = ⨿ Σ_{i0…in} (strict flags of length n) lies over Drap_n(I).

This page lists further axioms on these data.

(b) For i<j<k, Σ_ijk = Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk inside Σ_k. A priori only ⊂ holds.
- Equivalent form: for every z ∈ Σ_k, the down-set (Σ_*)_{≤z} → I_{≤k} is injective (29), and its order is the one induced from I_{≤k}.
- Margin generalisation: if d, d' are flags with the same end k and d'' = d ∪ d' is a flag, then Σ_{d''} = Σ_d ∩ Σ_{d'} in Σ_k.

(c) Disjointness.
- Main text: if i, j ≤ k have no common minorant, then Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk = ∅.
- Margin, sharper: if d, d' have the same end k and d ∪ d' is not a flag, then Σ_d ∩ Σ_d' = ∅. For d = (i,k) and d' = (j,k) this says Σ_ik and Σ_jk meet only when i and j are comparable.
- Together with (b), each z ∈ Σ_k lies on a set of faces Σ_ik whose indices form a chain. So (Σ_*)_{≤z} is a chain in I_{≤k}.

(d) Transversality (30). For k fixed, the subspaces Σ_ik (i < k) of Σ_k are transversal. For a flag d = (i1,…,in,k), the Σ_{i_r k} meet transversally along Σ_{i1…in k}.

So the following page can conclude that, under non-singularity:
- each Σ_k is a manifold with boundary (in fact with corners);
- the Σ_d with d ending at k are its corner strata, forming a 'cylindrical stratification' of the boundary;
- each face Σ_ik fibres over Σ_i (quasi-singularity), with fibres themselves stratified by products Dép(I_{i…j}) × Dép(I_{>j}).

In modern terms this is an axiomatisation of a 'manifold with fibred corners' / iterated fibration structure. Boundary hypersurfaces are indexed by lower strata. Two hypersurfaces meet only if their strata are comparable, and then they meet cornerwise and transversally. Each hypersurface fibres over the resolution of the smaller stratum, compatibly with the flag-indexed nerve.

Purpose: to give a combinatorial-geometric description of the 'déploiement' of a tame stratified space, as a diagram over flags of I, from which X is recovered by collapsing. This is presumably aimed at the equivalence 'tame stratified spaces ↔ déployed systems' announced in the Esquisse.
errors: The main-text version of condition (c) ('no common minorant ⇒ empty intersection') is weaker than the margin version ('d ∪ d' not a flag ⇒ empty'). Only the latter, i.e. comparability, gives the corner structure used on the next page. The main text and margin are inconsistent; the margin is the correct axiom.

The previous page's condition, transcribed as 'il existe un plus[?] un x … surjectif', must be 'au plus un x', i.e. injectivity of Σ_{≤z} → I_{≤j}. This matches (29) on this page. Surjectivity would force every face to be all of Σ_j.

The text's 'ce qui signifie aussi' bundles two things into (28). Injectivity of the down-set is the 'at most one' condition. (28) is the further statement that the order on the down-set is induced from I. The equivalence is fine once both are stated, but they are separate conditions.

Transversality (d) is stated only loosely ('localement … transversaux'). No regularity framework is specified (smooth? topological with collars?), so the conclusion 'manifold with corners' on the next page is heuristic here.

ideas.what: Encoding the unfolding of a stratified space as a topological category/simplicial space over the poset I. Objects are Σ_* = ⨿Σ_i, arrows Σ_ij, and the nerve Σ(n) = ⨿Σ_{i0…in} lies over strict flags of I.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of (generalized homotopy) links indexed by the subdivision sd(I); exit-path / décollage description of stratified homotopy types
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths); Douteau and Haine (diagrams of links over sd(P), ~2018–2021)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces a theory of 'déploiements' of tame stratified spaces, but not these axioms explicitly

ideas.what: Axioms (b) and (c): Σ_d'' = Σ_d ∩ Σ_d' when d ∪ d' is a flag, and Σ_d ∩ Σ_d' = ∅ otherwise. Faces of Σ_k indexed by I_{<k} meet only along chains.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary hypersurfaces of a resolved stratum indexed by lower strata, intersecting only for comparable strata ('manifold with fibred corners', ⟨n⟩-manifold-like face structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Davis (G-manifolds as collections of fibre bundles, 1978); Verona (1984); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka unzip (2017)

ideas.what: Condition (d): the faces Σ_ik ⊂ Σ_k are transversal, so Σ_{i1…in k} is their transversal intersection, a corner of codimension n.
ideas.modern_name: Manifold with corners whose corner strata are indexed by flags; Jänich/Laures ⟨n⟩-manifold condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jänich (1968), Laures (2000); Melrose school for the resolution of stratified spaces

ideas.what: Reformulation of (28) as: for each z ∈ Σ_k, the down-set (Σ_*)_{≤z} embeds order-preservingly in I_{≤k} (and by (c) is a chain).
ideas.modern_name: Local poset/chain condition for points of a resolved stratum (each point lies on a chain of faces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Melrose's iterated fibration structures and in Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the unfolded stratified space at once as (1) a topological category over I whose nerve is indexed by flags of I, and (2) a system of manifolds with fibred corners satisfying intersection/transversality axioms over flags. The two later lineages that realise these separately rarely make this link explicit with axioms like his. Those lineages are (1) the Douteau/Haine diagrams of links over sd(P), and (2) the Melrose/ALMP resolution with iterated fibration structure / Ayala–Francis–Tanaka unzip.
missed.quote: Σ_* → I … Σ_{*≤z} ↪ I_{≤k} injective … Σ_{ik} ∩ Σ_{jk} = ∅ … les Σ_{i1,k},…,Σ_{in,k} dans Σ_k sont des sous-espaces … transversaux le long de Σ_d
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The explicit flag-indexed axioms (b)–(d) give a clean combinatorial definition of a 'déployé' system. It could serve as a bridge for proving equivalences between conically smooth or Thom–Mather stratified spaces and corner-structured resolutions, phrased homotopy-theoretically via sd(I). This is mostly anticipated by Davis/Verona/ALMP/AFT, so the novelty is modest.

missed.claim: The axioms are stated, but the reconstruction of X from the system, and the claimed equivalence of categories, are not carried out on this page.
missed.quote: On suppose enfin que la synthèse des Σ_{ik} … sont transversaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is part of the never-written 'théorie des déploiements' announced in the Esquisse. Its later realisations are by other authors, without credit to these notes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful axiomatisation of the 'déploiement' as a manifold-with-fibred-corners system indexed by flags, dating from 1981–82. The ideas are anticipated by M. Davis (1978) and Verona (1984) and later systematised by ALMP and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; the déploiement idea itself is announced in the Esquisse. The explicit nerve/topological-category packaging over flags, linked to the corner axioms, is a notable unpublished detail but not a genuinely new result.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: 'il existe un plus[?] un x' should read 'il existe au plus un x'. Accordingly the margin 'Σ_{≤z} → I_{≤j} surjectif' is doubtful (the matching condition is injectivity).
'l'homo[?] d'ens.[?]' is probably 'l'homomorphisme d'ensembles ordonnés' Σ_* → I.
'l'ordre de (Σ_*)_z' should be 'l'ordre de (Σ_*)_{≤z} est induit par celui de I_{≤k}'.
'la synthèse des Σ_{ik}' is likely 'le système des Σ_{ik}'.
'Gros[?] d, d'' in the main text and margin is likely 'Cond. (c)' / 'Condition (c)'.
Top-left margin: the intersection Σ_{d''} = Σ_d ∩ Σ_{d'} should be taken 'dans Σ_k' (the common end), not 'dans Σ_i'.
(30): 'les Σ_{i,k}, Σ_{i2 k}…' should be 'les Σ_{i1 k}, Σ_{i2 k}, …, Σ_{in k}'.
